claims.text: GDACS's event report for 'Flood in Sri Lanka' (event id 1104075, source GLOFAS, overall Green alert, reporting window 02 Aug 2026 01:00 UTC to 04 Aug 2026 01:00 UTC) records via its Sendai indicator feed: 8 fatalities in Sri Lanka and 4 fatalities specifically in Hatton (12 total); 3,316 people evacuated plus 3,566 more evacuated (6,882 total); 15,412 people / 1,512 households affected; 537 and 129 buildings damaged (666 total); and 21 people rescued in Gampola.

Re-checked 8 August 2026: GDACS's event report (FL 1104075, episode 1) is unchanged — the same 2-4 August 2026 reporting window, 12 confirmed deaths and 6,882 evacuated via the Sendai indicator feed; no episode 2 or newer figures have been published.

Re-checked 9 August 2026: GDACS's Sendai indicator feed for event FL 1104075 was refreshed at 08:00:35 UTC today; the summed figures are unchanged at 12 fatalities (8 general + 4 in Hatton) and 6,882 evacuated (3,316 + 3,566), with 15,412 people/1,512 households affected and 666 buildings damaged. No episode 2 has been published.

Re-checked 10 August 2026: GDACS's event report for this flood event (eventid 1104075, episode 1) remains last updated 6 August 2026, with no Episode 2 issued. Death toll (12) and displaced figure (6,882) are unchanged.

Re-checked 11 August 2026 via direct fetch: the report remains at reporting window 02 Aug 2026 01:00 UTC to 04 Aug 2026 01:00 UTC, Episode 1, overall Green Flood alert (GDACS ID FL 1104075); the Sendai indicator feed figures are unchanged at 12 deaths and 6,882 displaced. No Episode 2 has been published.

Re-checked 12 August 2026: GDACS's event report for FL 1104075 (event id 1104075) remains at episode 1, reporting window 2-4 August 2026, overall Green alert; a careful re-fetch found no episode 2 link, and a targeted search found no evidence of one. Sendai indicator figures are unchanged: 12 deaths, 6,882 evacuated. GDACS has now held this event at Green/episode 1 with static figures for 6 consecutive days (6-12 August).

Sri Lanka's Disaster Management Centre, Situation Report dated 13 August 2026 at 1000hrs: Grand Total across 14 districts / 8 provinces -- 4,203 families (16,520 people) affected, 9 deaths, 7 injured, 0 missing, 2 houses fully damaged, 707 houses partially damaged, and 263 persons (73 families) currently in 12 safe locations, down from 495 persons (130 families) in the 11 August 2026 1000hrs report. This is the national government's own, more current ground-assessed figure; it supersedes the GDACS Sendai-feed snapshot (12 deaths, static since 6 August), which has not been updated to a new episode since.

DMC Situation Report — Sri Lanka, 14 August 2026 at 1000hrs: GRAND TOTAL — 4,209 Families / 16,536 People Affected; Deaths 9; Injured People 7; Missing People 0; Houses Damaged: 2 Fully, 713 Partially; Safe Location: 9 No. of Safety Locations, 52 Families, 188 Persons.

description: Heavy monsoon rainfall triggered flooding and landslides across Sri Lanka's central highlands beginning around 2 August 2026, affecting Kandy, Nuwara Eliya, Kegalle and Ratnapura districts, with the town of Hatton (Nuwara Eliya District) singled out for a fatal landslide. GDACS assessed the event as an overall Green alert (low humanitarian impact) for a reporting window of 2-4 August 2026, but its Sendai indicator feed records 12 confirmed deaths and about 6,882 people evacuated, alongside 15,412 people (1,512 households) affected and 666 buildings damaged. The disaster drew sustained international coverage given the region's continuing recovery from Cyclone Ditwah (November 2025), with authorities ordering school closures and military-assisted evacuations in affected districts. No allowlisted source has declared the event resolved. Re-checked 8 August 2026: GDACS's event report (FL 1104075, episode 1) is unchanged — the same 2-4 August 2026 reporting window, 12 confirmed deaths and 6,882 evacuated via the Sendai indicator feed; no episode 2 or newer figures have been published. Re-checked 9 August 2026: GDACS's event report (FL 1104075, episode 1) was refreshed at 08:00 UTC today but its Sendai indicator figures are unchanged — 12 confirmed deaths (8 general + 4 in Hatton) and 6,882 evacuated (3,316 + 3,566); no episode 2 has been published. Re-checked 10 August 2026: GDACS's report (episode 1) remains last updated 6 August 2026 with no newer episode issued; figures (12 deaths, 6,882 displaced) are unchanged. Re-checked 11 August 2026: direct fetch of GDACS's event report confirms it remains episode 1, reporting window 2-4 August 2026, with fatalities (12) and displaced (6,882) figures unchanged; no episode 2 has been published, and no newer allowlisted narrative sitrep for this event was found. Re-checked 12 August 2026: GDACS's event report is unchanged (Green alert, episode 1, 12 deaths, 6,882 evacuated), now static for 6 consecutive days; no episode 2 has been published and no allowlisted source has issued a closure or containment statement. Sri Lanka's Disaster Management Centre -- the national authority now issuing fresh, dated situation reports at least twice weekly -- reports 9 confirmed deaths and 0 missing as of 13 August 2026, revising down the earlier GDACS-sourced count of 12 deaths (static since 6 August), and shows the currently-sheltered population declining sharply, from 495 people (130 families) on 11 August to 263 people (73 families) on 13 August, with no new deaths reported in that window. Re-checked 14 August 2026: Sri Lanka's Disaster Management Centre situation report (14 August 2026, 1000hrs) reports 9 deaths and 7 injured, unchanged from 13 August, with the sheltered population continuing to decline — 188 persons (52 families) in 9 safe locations, down from 263 persons (73 families) on 13 August — while affected families/houses-damaged figures ticked up slightly (4,209 families/16,536 people affected; 713 houses partially damaged, up from 707). GDACS's event report (FL 1104075, episode 1) remains unchanged and static since 6 August.

impact.summary: GDACS's event report for Flood in Sri Lanka (event id 1104075, GLOFAS-sourced, reporting window 2-4 August 2026, overall Green alert) records, via its Sendai indicator feed (fetched 7 August 2026): 8 fatalities in Sri Lanka generally plus 4 fatalities specifically in Hatton (Nuwara Eliya District) -- 12 in total; 3,316 people evacuated plus a further 3,566 evacuated -- 6,882 in total; 15,412 people (1,512 households) affected; and 666 buildings damaged (537 in one indicator entry, 129 in another). 21 people were rescued in Gampola.
